statement: There is an infinite ordered tree with the maps, points, and positive weights described above. Each nonroot node v also has a budget ev > 0, a functional fv ∈ X∗ with ∥fv∥ ≤ 1, and the finite earlier-candidate list and predictions just defined. These data have the following properties: 11 1. The budgets satisfy ∑ v̸=r ev ≤ 1 128 . (4.6) Define τ0 = 1 2 , τk = 2−k−1 min{eu : u ∈ Li, 1 ≤ i ≤ k} (k ≥ 1). (4.7) Every node u ∈ Lk satisfies ∥ ∑ v̂=u αvyv − x∥ ≤ τk. (4.8) 2. For every nonroot node v, ∑ p≺v ∥Gp(yv) − yv∥ ≤ ev, fv(yv − z) ≥ 1 − ev (z ∈ Ev). (4.9) In particular, the second inequality holds at every zi with i ≤ k when v ∈ Lk. The budgets, functionals, and prediction sets assigned to retained nodes remain fixed when the remaining weights at their level and all later levels are chosen.
